text:
**Short answer: a power station of about 1,000 Wh is the sweet spot for a full night with a standard electric blanket.** I'd pick the **BLUETTI Elite 100 V2** (1,024 Wh).

**Why a ~1 kWh unit works**
- Blankets draw little power. The [Tested Watts guide](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/24/power-station-electric-blanket/) cites the Department of Energy figures of about 60 W for a single and 100 W for a double. At 100 W, a 1,024 Wh unit runs the blanket for about 8 hours. A 1,500 W space heater would drain the same unit in about 35 minutes.
- [Blackoutwise](https://www.blackoutwise.com/will-it-run/electric-blanket) says a queen blanket is rated about 150 W but cycles to an average of about 75 W. On that basis, 1,000 Wh runs it for 11–12 hours.
- [Blackoutwise's roundup](https://www.blackoutwise.com/best/best-power-station-for-electric-blanket) names the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 its top pick. It says the unit runs a 150 W blanket for about 12 hours, costs roughly $380–$500, and weighs 25 lb.

**Other options**
- **EcoFlow Delta 3 Classic (1,024 Wh):** This is similar in capacity. [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/pro/this-ecoflow-delta-3-classic-bundle-is-the-home-backup-battery-id-keep-ready-for-winter-storms-and-its-usd119-off-at-best-buy) lists a bundle with a 45W solar panel at $479 (was $598) at Best Buy. It has an LFP battery, 1,800W output, and a five-year warranty. TechRadar hasn't tested this model itself. The 45W panel is too small to recharge it quickly, and it weighs 26.7 lb.
- **Budget, single blanket:** [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-heated-blanket-all-night) recommends the BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 (288 Wh, $289.99). It only works for a 12 V blanket on low from the car port. [Blackoutwise](https://www.blackoutwise.com/best/best-power-station-for-electric-blanket) says a 288 Wh unit runs a 150 W blanket for only about 3–3.5 hours, so it won't cover a night with a standard 120 V blanket.
- **Two nights, or a blanket plus other gear:** Blackoutwise says the Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 runs the same blanket for about 23 hours.

**Caveats**
- Estimates vary a lot. [HomePowerFacts](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/electric-blanket/) assumes a conservative 260 W average draw for a queen blanket. That would require about 2,600 Wh for 8 hours. Check your blanket's wattage label. If it's on the high end and you run it on high all night, size up.
- If you also run a CPAP, Blackoutwise says the two together average about 109 W. A 1,024 Wh unit lasts about 8 hours at that draw.
- Plug the blanket directly into the station. Don't use extension cords or power strips, and keep the station off the bed ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-heated-blanket-all-night)).

If you tell me your blanket's size and wattage, I can narrow this down.
